subject: Long-term rate stability + tiered repricing proposal for Avalon Analytics
messages:
From: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@avalon.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@avalon.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — request to firm up protections

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the KV caching approach. Before we move to an internal procurement review, our CFO wants clearer language on pricing stability for a committed-volume deal. Specifically she asked for: 1) an annual CPI cap tied to the US CPI (so per-token rates can't increase > X%/year), 2) an MFN-like assurance across your hosted catalog for equivalent commitment tiers, and 3) clarity on how repricing works if our usage materially exceeds the committed tier (step-up discounts vs overage rates).

I've attached our Q1–Q3 usage export to show expected consumption patterns — it skews spiky with seasonal peaks. Can Redwood propose contract language for those three items and indicate any operational constraints (e.g., burst capacity pricing, roll-forward true-ups)? We also want to understand how long the price lock applies after a committed term (renewal mechanics).

Our timeline: procurement wants final terms by the end of next week to make the July board review.

Appreciate the help — cc'ing Tom (procurement) who will coordinate the internal redlines.

Best,
Sofia
Head of Product Partnerships
Avalon Analytics

Attachment: Avalon_Usage_Profile_Q1-3.csv (csv, 48KB)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@avalon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — request to firm up protections

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sending the usage file. High level: we can accommodate a combination of annual CPI cap + a commitment-tier MFN for comparable customers, but there are a few tradeoffs to be explicit about so we set expectations with finance/legal:

- CPI cap: we can cap annual list-price increases to a fixed percentage above the US CPI (e.g., CPI + 2pp) for the duration of the committed term. That cap applies to list per-token pricing for hosted API models; it does not apply to pass-through cloud infra costs or to changes in model family pricing that materially change compute characteristics.
- MFN: we can agree to a best-available-price guarantee among hosted token-tier customers for identical commitment and term length. This is operationally feasible for hosted-only (not for dedicated/private). MFN would require a clear definition of "equivalent commitment tier" (tokens/month, term length).
- Overages & step-up: we typically use a tiered step-up model: if monthly usage exceeds the committed tier by >20% for 2 consecutive months, pricing auto-moves to the next tier (with pro-rated discounts), otherwise overage is billed at the committed tier rate + fixed overage premium. We can also offer a true-up at quarter end so spikes won't immediately trigger permanent repricing unless sustained.

I'll ask Ben and Marissa to draft proposed contract language and a numeric example that maps to your CSV so procurement has a clear P&L for different scenarios.

Quick Qs for you: what CPI series should we anchor to (US CPI-U is typical), and do you want MFN to be back-dated (apply retroactively) or prospective only?

I'll aim to get a first redline by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — request to firm up protections

Eve / Marissa —

Looping in a draft approach for legal and finance to review (summary + redline to follow):

1) Price lock mechanics
- Term: price lock applies during the committed term (we typically do 12 or 24 months). On renewal, we can extend a lock for an additional term if Avalon rolls to an equal or higher committed tier.
- CPI cap: propose "Per-token list prices for the Hosted API will not increase by more than the greater of 0% or the US All Urban Consumers CPI-U year-over-year increase plus 2 percentage points in any contract year."

2) MFN clause (hosted only)
- Language: "During the committed term, if Redwood offers a lower Hosted API per-token list price to any other customer with substantially similar committed volume and term length, Redwood will extend that lower per-token list price to Avalon prospectively within 30 days."
- We should limit MFN to 'substantially similar' deals to avoid perverse sequencing — legal will want precise metrics (within ±10% of tokens and same term length).

3) Overages / step-up / true-up
- Two buckets: (a) short spikes (<=2 months in a rolling 3-month window) = billed as overage at committed rate + 15% premium with quarter-end true-up; (b) sustained increases (>2 months consecutive beyond 20% threshold) = automatic tier step-up with pro-rated discounts and a new committed tier effective at start of next billing month.

4) Additional operational notes
- Burst capacity: available at published burst rates; bursts don't change committed pricing unless sustained.
- Reporting & audit: provide monthly token-level usage with delta analysis; Avalon can request a one-time audit per year if needed.

I'll attach a redline with suggested wording and examples. If procurement wants retroactive MFN (apply to prior invoices), legal will push back — we can discuss a limited look-back window (e.g., 30 days) as a compromise.

Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-rate-guardrails-redline.docx (docx, 12KB)
From: Tom Chen <tom.chen@avalon.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@avalon.ai>, "CFO - Avalon (procurement@avalon.ai)" <procurement@avalon.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — request to firm up protections

Evelyn / Ben —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A few clarifications from procurement/CFO:

- CPI anchor: we'll use US CPI-U, annual release. CFO wants the cap to be absolute (e.g., no more than +3%/year) rather than CPI + X to simplify forecasting. Would Redwood accept a hard cap of 3%/yr for a 24-month term if Avalon commits to a min of 18B tokens over the first year?
- MFN: prospective-only is acceptable. Procurement will accept a ±15% comparability band for tokens and same term length, but wants MFN to include any 'promotional' transient discounts (short-term price reductions) for the same product class.
- Overages: quarter-end true-up is workable. For the auto step-up, procurement requests a 30-day notice before new tier pricing applies to allow internal budget adjustments.

We can fast-track if Redwood can confirm the 3% hard cap for a 24-month commitment at the volumes above. If that's a no-go we can look at CPI-U + 1% instead.

Tom
Head of Procurement (interim)
Avalon Analytics
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@avalon.ai>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@avalon.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed compromise language + examples (see attached)

Hi Sofia / Tom —

Great alignment so far. Per internal legal/finance feedback, here's a pragmatic compromise we can offer to meet Avalon procurement timing:

1) CPI cap: Redwood will accept a fixed cap of 3% per contract year for a 24-month term if Avalon signs for a minimum committed consumption of 18B tokens in year 1. If Avalon takes a 12-month term we can do CPI-U + 1% instead.

2) MFN: prospective-only MFN within a ±15% token comparability band and same term length. MFN will include promotional, temporary price reductions only if the promotional pricing was published and applied to the deal class for a minimum of 14 days. No retroactive invoice credits beyond a 30-day lookback window.

3) Overages / step-up: maintain the quarter-end true-up approach. For automatic tier step-up we will provide a 30-calendar-day notice prior to the new tier pricing taking effect; during that notice period Avalon may elect a one-time 30-day grace for backlog smoothing.

Attached is a redline with the exact proposed wording, plus three numeric scenarios mapping to your usage (spike month, sustained growth, and steady-state). If that looks good we can prepare an SOW and finalize commercial terms for procurement.

Two quick asks from our side: 1) confirm the required billing currency (USD) and 2) confirm whether Avalon needs any specific escrow or audit SLA language — that would be an add-on.

If you want to jump on a 30-minute call today to lock numbers for board, I can join.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts, EMEA & US
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-rate-guardrails-redline.docx (docx, 12KB); Avalon_Usage_Profile_Q1-3.csv (csv, 48KB)
